newsitem.title: GERMANY: Disney sells stake in German Tele-Muenchen.
newsitem.headline: Disney sells stake in German Tele-Muenchen.

text.p: German media executive Herbert Kloiber has bought back the 50 percent stake in his film group Tele-Muenchen Gruppe (TMG) that was held by U.S. media giant Walt Disney Co, company officials said on Thursday.

Officials at TMG told Reuters that Kloiber is once again the company's only shareholder since Capital Cities first bought 50 percent of the company eight years ago. The sale of the stake follows the merger of Disney and ABC/Capital Cities.
The main reason for pulling out of Tele-Muenchen was a conflict in dealing with film licences and distribution between Disney and Kloiber.

"A conflict of interest has evolved through the merger of Disney and ABC/Capital Cities," said Kloiber in a telephone interview. "As a major company Disney operates an integrated marketing system in Europe."
Disney and Tele-Muenchen remain equal shareholders in Tele-Muenchen Media, the holding company for their interests in TV stations RTL2 and TM3, a nationally broadcast channel for women.
